claim: Gasdermin-D (GSDMD) is the ultimate effector of pyroptosis, a form of programmed cell death associated with pathogen invasion and inflammation.
source: Gasdermin-D (GSDMD) is the ultimate effector of pyroptosis, a form of programmed cell death associated with pathogen invasion and inflammation.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about GSDMD's role in pyroptosis.

claim: After proteolytic cleavage by caspases, the GSDMD N-terminal domain (GSDMDNT) assembles on the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane and induces the formation of membrane pores.
source: After proteolytic cleavage by caspases, the GSDMD N-terminal domain (GSDMDNT) assembles on the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane and induces the formation of membrane pores.
evidence: This is established knowledge about GSDMD mechanism of action.

claim: GSDMDNT has distinct interaction motifs with phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) and phosphatidylserine (PS) headgroups.
source: We identify distinct interaction motifs of GSDMDNT with phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) and phosphatidylserine (PS) headgroups and describe their conformational dependence.
evidence: This claim is supported by data from the MD simulations presented in the manuscript.

claim: The lipid interaction motifs of GSDMDNT with PI(4,5)P2 and PS show conformational dependence.
source: We identify distinct interaction motifs of GSDMDNT with phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) and phosphatidylserine (PS) headgroups and describe their conformational dependence.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data showing different binding patterns in prepore vs pore conformations.

claim: Oligomers are stabilized by shared lipid binding sites between neighboring monomers acting akin to double-sided tape.
source: Oligomers are stabilized by shared lipid binding sites between neighboring monomers acting akin to double-sided tape.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data showing PI(4,5)P2 bridging between subunits.

claim: Small GSDMDNT oligomers support stable, water-filled, and ion-conducting membrane pores bounded by curled beta-sheets.
source: We show that already small GSDMDNT oligomers support stable, water-filled, and ion-conducting membrane pores bounded by curled beta-sheets.
evidence: This is directly supported by simulation data of oligomers from monomer to decamer.

claim: High-order GSDMDNT oligomers can crack under the line tension of 86 pN created by an open membrane edge.
source: We find that high-order GSDMDNT oligomers can crack under the line tension of 86 pN created by an open membrane edge to form the slit pores or closed GSDMDNT rings seen in atomic force microscopy experiments.
evidence: This is supported by simulation data showing arc cracking and calculated membrane edge tension.

claim: Sublytic pores formed by GSDMDNT explain nonselective ion flux during early pyroptosis.
source: Our simulations provide a detailed view of key steps in GSDMDNT-induced plasma membrane pore formation, including sublytic pores that explain nonselective ion flux during early pyroptosis.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation data showing ion permeation through small oligomeric pores and cited experimental observations.

claim: Pyroptosis leads to lysis of the affected cell and to the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) such as mature IL-1β and IL-18.
source: Pyroptosis is a recently discovered form of regulated cell death that leads to lysis of the affected cell and to the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) such as mature IL-1β and IL-18 (He et al., 2015; Tsuchiya et al., 2021; Xia et al., 2021; Xie et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Pyroptosis is tightly regulated by the assembly of canonical or non-canonical inflammasomes and the activation or presence of certain caspases, granzymes or pathogenic proteases.
source: Pyroptosis is tightly regulated by the assembly of canonical or non-canonical inflammasomes and the activation or presence of certain caspases, granzymes or pathogenic proteases (Shi et al., 2015; Kayagaki et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2021; Deng et al., 2022; Wen et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Proteases activate gasdermins by cleaving off their C-terminal domains, which exposes a basic surface on the N-terminal domain.
source: In turn, these proteases activate gasdermins by cleaving off their C-terminal domains, which exposes a basic surface on the N-terminal domain (Liu et al., 2021; Xia et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The N-terminal domain of gasdermin binds to the plasma membrane, oligomerizes, and inserts a β-sheet into the membrane, similar to bacterial β pore-forming toxins.
source: The N-terminal domain then binds to the plasma membrane, oligomerizes, and inserts a β-sheet into the membrane, similar to bacterial β pore-forming toxins (Dal Peraro and van der Goot, 2016) though acting from the inner leaflet.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Gasdermin acts from the inner leaflet of the membrane.
source: The N-terminal domain then binds to the plasma membrane, oligomerizes, and inserts a β-sheet into the membrane, similar to bacterial β pore-forming toxins (Dal Peraro and van der Goot, 2016) though acting from the inner leaflet.
evidence: This is established knowledge about gasdermin mechanism.

claim: The hydrophobic face of the β-sheet anchors the sheet into the membrane and its hydrophilic face facilitates the opening of an approximately 20 nm wide membrane pore.
source: The hydrophobic face of the β-sheet anchors the sheet into the membrane and its hydrophilic face facilitates the opening of an approximately 20 nm wide membrane pore (Ruan et al., 2018; Xia et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: The opening of the gasdermin pore in most cases leads to an osmotic shock that ultimately disrupts the integrity of the cell.
source: In addition to cytokine release, the opening of the pore in most cases leads to an osmotic shock that ultimately disrupts the integrity of the cell (Fink and Cookson, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Gasdermins play a crucial role in the innate immune response to pathogen infection.
source: Gasdermins play a crucial role in the innate immune response to pathogen infection.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about gasdermin function.

claim: Altered activation of pyroptosis has been associated with various types of cancers and cancer treatments.
source: Altered activation of pyroptosis has also been associated with various types of cancers and cancer treatments (Liu et al., 2021; Wu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Gasdermin-D (GSDMD) is the best-characterized gasdermin of the six human isoforms.
source: Gasdermin-D (GSDMD) is the best-characterized gasdermin of the six human isoforms.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the gasdermin family.

claim: GSDMD is expressed in many tissues, including cells of the gastrointestinal system, the circulatory system, the skin, the lung, and many immune cells.
source: It is expressed in many tissues, including cells of the gastrointestinal system, the circulatory system, the skin, the lung, and many immune cells (Broz et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: GSDMD's central role in infection response makes it a target of therapeutic applications.
source: Its central role in infection response makes GSDMD a target of therapeutic applications (Liu et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: After proteolytic cleavage, GSDMDNT binds specifically to negatively charged lipids of the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane.
source: After proteolytic cleavage, the GSDMD N-terminal domain (GSDMDNT) binds specifically to negatively charged lipids of the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane, where it forms β-pores comprising around 30 subunits (Aglietti et al., 2016; Ding et al., 2016; Liu et al., 2016; Xia et al., 2021; Mulvihill et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: GSDMDNT forms β-pores comprising around 30 subunits.
source: After proteolytic cleavage, the GSDMD N-terminal domain (GSDMDNT) binds specifically to negatively charged lipids of the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane, where it forms β-pores comprising around 30 subunits (Aglietti et al., 2016; Ding et al., 2016; Liu et al., 2016; Xia et al., 2021; Mulvihill et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: Cryo-electron microscopy studies resolved the pore structures of mouse gasdermin-A3 (GSDMA3) and human GSDMD.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) studies resolved the pore structures of mouse gasdermin-A3 (GSDMA3) (Ruan et al., 2018) and human GSDMD (Xia et al., 2021), respectively, and identified the density of a fully assembled prepore ring stacked opposite the pore structure and separated by detergent.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: Cryo-EM studies identified the density of a fully assembled prepore ring stacked opposite the pore structure and separated by detergent.
source: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) studies resolved the pore structures of mouse gasdermin-A3 (GSDMA3) (Ruan et al., 2018) and human GSDMD (Xia et al., 2021), respectively, and identified the density of a fully assembled prepore ring stacked opposite the pore structure and separated by detergent.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: AFM imaging resolved circular assemblies that could be washed off the supported bilayer.
source: Very recently, atomic force microscopy (AFM) imaging resolved circular assemblies that could be washed off the supported bilayer (Mari et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: AFM experiments of growing assemblies and the observation of nonselective ion influx and efflux in the early phases of pyroptosis favor an alternative pore assembly pathway in which GSDMDNT first forms membrane-inserted arcs and slits.
source: On the other hand, AFM experiments of growing assemblies (Mulvihill et al., 2018) and the observation of nonselective ion influx and efflux in the early phases of pyroptosis (de Vasconcelos et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2016) favor an alternative pore assembly pathway, in which GSDMDNT first forms membrane-inserted arcs and slits, which can then grow over time to build full circular pores (Rühl and Broz, 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior experimental observations.

claim: GSDMDNT strongly interacted with acidic lipids in all simulations of the prepore and pore conformations.
source: GSDMDNT strongly interacted with acidic lipids in all our simulations of the prepore and pore conformations.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: Noticeable enrichment of lipids with acidic phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) and phosphatidylserine (PS) headgroups around the protein was observed during the equilibration phase.
source: We observed noticeable enrichment of lipids with acidic phosphatidylinositol-4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) and phosphatidylserine (PS) headgroups around the protein already during the equilibration phase.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: Anionic lipids interacted more strongly with GSDMDNT than expected based on their abundance in the inner leaflet compared to zwitterionic lipids.
source: In comparison to zwitterionic lipids (phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) and phosphatidylcholine (PC)), anionic lipids interacted more strongly with GSDMDNT than what would naïvely be expected based on their abundance in the inner leaflet (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The enrichment of the anionic PS and PI(4,5)P2 lipids continued during the production phase, resulting in the formation of distinct clusters at the protein underside.
source: In the production phase of the MD simulations, the enrichment of the anionic PS and PI(4,5)P2 lipids continued, resulting in the formation of distinct clusters at the protein underside, stabilized by abundant basic amino acids.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: The β1–β2 loop (residues 42–55) emerged as a focal point of interactions with anionic lipids.
source: The β1–β2 loop (residues 42–55; numbering as in the cryo-EM structure by Xia et al., 2021) emerged as a focal point of interactions with anionic lipids (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is supported by simulation data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Aromatic residues W48, F49, W50, and Y54 anchored the β1–β2 loop deeply into the upper membrane leaflet.
source: Its aromatic residues W48, F49, W50, and Y54 anchored the loop deeply into the upper membrane leaflet.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: Anionic lipids clustered at the interface of the β1–β2 loop with the α1 helix, dominated by interactions with R10, K51, R53.
source: Anionic lipids clustered at the interface of the β1–β2 loop with the α1 helix (dominated by interactions with R10, K51, R53), the α3 helix (dominated by interactions with K43, R53, K55, R153), and the disordered C-terminus (dominated by interactions with K51, K235, K236, R238).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: An additional binding site for anionic lipids between α1 and β7 was stabilized by interactions with R7, R10, R11, and R178.
source: An additional binding site for anionic lipids between α1 and β7 was stabilized by interactions with R7, R10, R11, and R178.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: In around two thirds of interfaces between neighboring subunits in the 33-mer pore, a PI(4,5)P2 headgroup interacted with both neighbors at the same time.
source: In around two thirds of interfaces between neighboring subunits in the 33-mer pore, we found a PI(4,5)P2 headgroup that interacted with both neighbors at the same time (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The flexible, unfolded hairpins of the prepore 33-mer appear to stabilize bridging PI(4,5)P2 between neighboring subunits.
source: The flexible, unfolded hairpins of the prepore 33-mer appear to stabilize bridging PI(4,5)P2 between neighboring subunits.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations of PI(4,5)P2 bridging patterns.

claim: In the prepore monomer, the α1 helix was tilted at an angle of ≈30° with respect to the membrane plane, with the N-terminus pointing towards the membrane.
source: By contrast, in the prepore monomer the α1 helix was tilted at an angle of ≈30° with respect to the membrane plane, with the N-terminus pointing towards the membrane (Figure 1A, dark blue).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In the pore conformation, the α1 helices formed a continuous belt lying flat on the membrane.
source: In the pore conformation, the α1 helices (Figure 1B, dark blue) formed a continuous belt lying flat on the membrane.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In the prepore conformation, the 33-mer complex maintained a nearly circular shape and remained tightly bound to the intracellular leaflet of the plasma membrane for the entirety of the 3.5 µs simulation.
source: In the prepore conformation, the 33-mer complex maintained a nearly circular shape and remained tightly bound to the intracellular leaflet of the plasma membrane for the entirety of the 3.5 µs simulation (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Within the first nanoseconds of the production simulation, the originally folded β-hairpins of the prepore 33-mer unfolded and the ring deformed the membrane upwards into a crown shape.
source: Within the first nanoseconds of the production simulation, its originally folded β-hairpins unfolded and the ring deformed the membrane upwards into a crown shape (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In the pore conformation, GSDMDNT stabilized a 21.6 nm wide, water-filled pore with a fully intact β-sheet lining its side.
source: In the pore conformation, GSDMDNT stabilized a 21.6 nm wide, water-filled pore with a fully intact β-sheet lining its side (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 2C and D.

claim: During the entire 5 µs simulation of the pore conformation, the membrane remained flat.
source: During the entire simulation (5 µs), the membrane remained flat (Figure 2D), which is in contrast to the prepore ring.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Around the tips of the inserted hairpins the membrane was thinned because the hairpins are not long enough to reach fully across the membrane to the lipid headgroups of the extracellular leaflet.
source: However, around the tips of the inserted hairpins the membrane was thinned because the hairpins are not long enough to reach fully across the membrane to the lipid headgroups of the extracellular leaflet.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data and explained by structural constraints.

claim: In the simulation of a pore initially filled with a lipid bilayer, the lipid patch blocking the pore detached from the hydrophilic inside of the membrane-spanning β-sheet already during the equilibration phase.
source: In this simulation, the lipid patch blocking the pore detached from the hydrophilic inside of the membrane-spanning β-sheet already during the equilibration phase (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A bicelle-like plug formed that then started to tilt and moved slowly in the direction of the intracellular space along the protein surface.
source: A bicelle-like plug formed that then started to tilt. As it tilted, the plug moved slowly in the direction of the intracellular space along the protein surface (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 3B and C.

claim: All GSDMDNT systems, including the monomer, remained stably inserted in the membrane for the entirety of the simulations, independent of the number of subunits.
source: Independent of the number of subunits, all GSDMDNT systems, including the monomer, remained stably inserted in the membrane for the entirety of our simulations (Figure 4A–F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 4A-F.

claim: All oligomeric systems maintained a continuous water column on the pore-facing side of the inserted β-sheet.
source: While the water chains along the small sheet of monomeric GSDMDNT were regularly interrupted, all oligomeric systems maintained a continuous water column on the pore-facing side of the inserted β-sheet.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: Sodium and chloride ions permeated in both directions through the water-filled oligomeric pores.
source: Sodium and chloride ions permeated in both directions through the water-filled oligomeric pores (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The number of ion permeation events increased with oligomer size.
source: The number of permeation events increased with oligomer size.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: In systems with two or more GSDMDNT, the β-sheet curled up to form pores.
source: In systems with two or more GSDMDNT, we found that the β-sheet curled up to form pores (Figure 4B–F).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 4B-F.

claim: The edge of the sheet formed by the β3 strand stayed normal to the membrane plane.
source: Whereas the edge of the sheet formed by the β3 strand stayed normal to the membrane plane, the other end of the sheet formed by the β7–β8 hairpin tilted upwards to an angle of ≈55° and almost crossed the membrane plane (Figure 4C and E, front view).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 4C and E.

claim: The end of the sheet formed by the β7–β8 hairpin tilted upwards to an angle of ≈55° and almost crossed the membrane plane.
source: Whereas the edge of the sheet formed by the β3 strand stayed normal to the membrane plane, the other end of the sheet formed by the β7–β8 hairpin tilted upwards to an angle of ≈55° and almost crossed the membrane plane (Figure 4C and E, front view).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 4C and E.

claim: In the GSDMDNT 16-mer and 27-mer simulations, the plasma membrane lipids receded quickly from the hydrophilic face of the β-sheet, often already during the equilibration steps.
source: In the GSDMDNT 16-mer and 27-mer simulations (Figure 5A and B), the plasma membrane lipids receded quickly from the hydrophilic face of the β-sheet, often already during the equilibration steps.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Water flowed into the space vacated by the lipids along the sheet in concert with lipid recession.
source: In concert, water flowed into the space vacated by the lipids along the sheet.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: Phospholipid headgroups wrapped around the open membrane edge to shield the otherwise exposed hydrophobic membrane core from water.
source: On the side of the receding membrane, phospholipid headgroups wrapped around the now open membrane edge to shield the otherwise exposed hydrophobic membrane core from water.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: Across the open edge, the intracellular and the extracellular membrane leaflets could exchange lipids.
source: Across the open edge, the intracellular and the extracellular membrane leaflets could exchange lipids.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: The 27-mer arc contraction resulted in the formation of a circular pore with a diameter of ≈17 nm within 4 μs.
source: In case of the 27-mer arc, this contraction resulted in the formation of a circular pore with a diameter of ≈17 nm within 4 μs (Figure 5B, Figure 5—video 2).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In all simulations of oligomers comprising between 5 and 16 subunits, the initial arcs cracked at the center as the membrane edge shortened and contacts between the globular domains of neighboring subunits were lost.
source: By contrast, in all simulations of oligomers comprising between 5 and 16 subunits, the initial arcs cracked at the center as the membrane edge shortened and contacts between the globular domains of neighboring subunits were lost (Table 1, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Table 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 16-mer cracked after ≈0.9 μs, which resulted in the formation of a kink in the arc.
source: The 16-mer cracked after ≈0.9 μs, which resulted in the formation of a kink in the arc (Figure 5A, Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Despite the loss of contacts between the globular domains, the inserted β-sheets of all cracked arcs stayed fully intact, even in the highly curved cracked region of the pores.
source: Importantly, despite the loss of contacts between the globular domains, the inserted β-sheets of all cracked arcs stayed fully intact, even in the highly curved cracked region of the pores.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: For DOPC, a lower membrane edge tension of 44.3±2.1 pN has been reported.
source: For DOPC, a lower membrane edge tension of 44.3±2.1 pN (West et al., 2013) has been reported.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: In the DOPC membrane, lipids receded more rapidly from the inserted β-barrel to form a pore compared to the plasma membrane mimetic (within 400 ns).
source: Compared to the plasma membrane mimetic, the lipids receded more rapidly from the inserted β-barrel to form a pore (within 400 ns, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: As the membrane edge contracted in DOPC, the GSDMDNT arc cracked in three positions to form a nearly circular pore rather than the slit-shaped pore seen in the plasma membrane mimetic.
source: As the membrane edge contracted, the GSDMDNT arc cracked in three positions to form a nearly circular pore rather than the slit-shaped pore seen in the plasma membrane mimetic.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: The β1–β2 loop shares interaction sites with all of the other arginine and lysine rich sites.
source: In the MD simulations, we found that these basic patches do not act independently of each other. In particular, the flexible β1–β2 loop shares interaction sites with all of the other arginine and lysine rich sites.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: GSDMDNT binds the plasma membrane differently depending on whether it is in its monomeric prepore conformation or its oligomeric pore conformation.
source: In addition, our simulations revealed that GSDMDNT binds the plasma membrane differently, depending on whether it is in its monomeric prepore conformation or its oligomeric pore conformation.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data comparing prepore and pore conformations.

claim: Differences in the strength of membrane interactions may drive the reorientation of GSDMDNT on the membrane during the transition from prepore to pore conformation.
source: Differences in the strength of these interactions may drive the reorientation of GSDMDNT on the membrane during the transition from prepore to pore conformation.
evidence: This is speculated based on observed differences in lipid binding between conformations.

claim: K145, Q149, and R151 are involved in membrane binding but not pore formation.
source: The described differences also point to certain residues involved in membrane binding, but not pore formation, such as K145, Q149, and R151.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations of conformation-specific binding.

claim: In variants with K145 and R151 mutated to alanine, oligomerization and pyroptosis are compromised, as is localization to the detergent phase in lysed cells.
source: In variants with K145 and R151 mutated to alanine, oligomerization and pyroptosis are compromised, as is localization to the detergent phase in lysed cells (Liu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: Binding of a single PI(4,5)P2 to R7, R174, and R178 at the same time may kinetically trap these three residues in a distinct pore-like orientation long enough to facilitate the folding of the β-hairpin.
source: Furthermore, while entropically unfavorable, binding of a single PI(4,5)P2 to R7, R174, and R178 at the same time may kinetically trap these three residues in a distinct pore-like orientation long enough to facilitate the folding of the β-hairpin.
evidence: This is speculated based on observed binding patterns in simulations.

claim: The preference of gasdermins to form pores in membranes containing multivalent acidic lipids such as PI(4,5)P2, PI(3,4,5)P3, and cardiolipin may be explained by simultaneous binding of these lipids to multiple residues.
source: This may also explain the preference of gasdermins to form pores in membranes containing multivalent acidic lipids such as PI(4,5)P2, phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-triphosphate (PI(3,4,5)P3), and cardiolipin (Ding et al., 2016).
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations and cited experimental preferences.

claim: Bridging lipids acting as 'double-sided tapes' should facilitate oligomerization by attracting membrane-bound gasdermins and by helping to orientate them with respect to each other.
source: Even if the bridging lipids (Muller et al., 2019) acting as 'double-sided tapes' may not confer high mechanical strength to the multimerization interface, they should facilitate oligomerization by attracting membrane-bound gasdermins and by helping to orientate them with respect to each other.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations of bridging lipids and cited concept.

claim: The 33-mer in prepore conformation is more interconnected by PI(4,5)P2 than the 33-mer in pore conformation.
source: It is therefore also interesting to see that the 33-mer in prepore conformation is even more interconnected by PI(4,5)P2 than the 33-mer in pore conformation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Lipid-mediated interactions should facilitate prepore assembly on the plasma membrane, which is rich in PI(4,5)P2.
source: These lipid-mediated interactions should facilitate prepore assembly on the plasma membrane, which is rich in PI(4,5)P2.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations of lipid bridging and knowledge of membrane composition.

claim: The mechanism of joint binding sites and bridging lipids could provide an additional explanation for the preference of GSDMDNT for multivalent acidic lipids.
source: Combined with our observation of joint binding sites within one subunit, this mechanism could provide an additional explanation for the preference of GSDMDNT for multivalent acidic lipids (Ding et al., 2016) and for the recent observation that it shows less diverse pore conformations in PI(4,5)P2 or PI(3,4,5)P3 rich membranes than in pure PE/PC membranes (Santa Cruz Garcia et al., 2022).
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations and cited experimental observations.

claim: Prepore oligomers of pneumolysin (PLY) have been shown to recruit cholesterol, which locally enhanced lipid order.
source: Similar to the recruitment of PI(4,5)P2 by GSDMDNT, prepore oligomers of pneumolysin (PLY), a cholesterol dependent cytolysin (CDC), have been shown to recruit cholesterol, which locally enhanced lipid order (Faraj et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The membrane β-sheet of monomeric PLY was pushed out of the membrane within 1 µs in one of two atomistic replica simulations in earlier work.
source: In earlier work, we found that the membrane β-sheet of monomeric PLY was pushed out of the membrane within 1 µs in one of two atomistic replica simulations (Vögele et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior simulation work.

claim: The β-hairpins of monomeric and dimeric GSDMDNT stayed stably membrane inserted for the entirety of 5 µs simulations.
source: It was therefore surprising to us that the β-hairpins of monomeric and dimeric GSDMDNT stayed stably membrane inserted for the entirety of our 5 µs simulations.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: AFM experiments identified stable, presumably inserted, arcs of the CDC suilysin comprising as few as five subunits.
source: Combined with our observation of stable prepore oligomers and the identification of stable, presumably inserted, arcs of the CDC suilysin comprising as few as five subunits (Leung et al., 2014), this finding opens up the possibility that GSDMDNT inserts its β-sheet already from such small oligomers.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: GSDMDNT was shown to permit growth of inserted arcs.
source: In contrast to PLY, GSDMDNT was shown to permit growth of inserted arcs (Mulvihill et al., 2018) and we believe that such stably inserted small oligomers could diffuse together to form slit and ring-shaped pores (Leung et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: Stably inserted small oligomers could diffuse together to form slit and ring-shaped pores.
source: In contrast to PLY, GSDMDNT was shown to permit growth of inserted arcs (Mulvihill et al., 2018) and we believe that such stably inserted small oligomers could diffuse together to form slit and ring-shaped pores (Leung et al., 2014).
evidence: This is speculated based on simulation observations and cited experimental work.

claim: The fact that pores formed by small oligomers permit water and ion conduction across the membrane is in line with observed ion flux and size exclusion in the early phases of pyroptosis.
source: In addition, the fact that the pores formed by small oligomers already permit water and ion conduction across the membrane is perfectly in line with observed ion flux and size exclusion in the early phases of pyroptosis (de Vasconcelos et al., 2019; Chen et al., 2016; Rühl and Broz, 2022).
evidence: This is inferred from simulation data and cited experimental observations.

claim: Release of IL-1 family cytokines will require pores of at least 10 GSDMDNT subunits.
source: Sterically, release of IL-1 family cytokines (Kato et al., 2003; Finzel et al., 1989) will require pores of at least 10 GSDMDNT subunits.
evidence: This is inferred from cited structural information about cytokine size and simulation data on pore sizes.

claim: The interface between globular domains of neighboring subunits occasionally broke under stress.
source: Furthermore, we occasionally found the interface between globular domains of neighboring subunits to break under stress.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: The membrane inserted β-sheet always stayed intact, even in the highly curved kink region of slit-shaped pores.
source: By contrast, the membrane inserted β-sheet always stayed intact, even in the highly curved kink region of slit-shaped pores.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: The remarkable stability of the β-sheet and adaption to high curvature suggests that β-sheet formation may stabilize GSDMDNT oligomers in pore conformation.
source: This remarkable stability of the β-sheet and adaption to high curvature suggests that β-sheet formation may stabilize GSDMDNT oligomers in pore conformation.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations of β-sheet stability.

claim: Mulvihill et al., 2018 identified an abundance of membrane inserted slit-shaped pores in AFM experiments.
source: In AFM experiments, Mulvihill et al., 2018 identified an abundance of membrane inserted slit-shaped pores.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: Santa Cruz Garcia et al., 2022 discovered that GSDMDNT pores may be able to dynamically open and close.
source: Recently, Santa Cruz Garcia et al., 2022 discovered that GSDMDNT pores may be able to dynamically open and close and they discuss that slit-shaped pores may provide the closed state to which open rings can collapse.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior experimental work.

claim: Slit-shaped pores can form spontaneously from arcs, driven by the tension along an open membrane edge.
source: We further show that slit-shaped pores can form spontaneously from arcs, driven by the tension along an open membrane edge.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data.

claim: Already monomers and small oligomers can support stable membrane insertion.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that already monomers and small oligomers can support stable membrane insertion.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation data showing stable insertion of small oligomers.

claim: Similar to the α pore-forming toxin ClyA, smaller inserted oligomers may fuse with one another to build larger slit and finally ring-shaped pores.
source: Similar to the α pore-forming toxin ClyA, these smaller inserted oligomers may fuse with one another to build larger slit and finally ring-shaped pores (Benke et al., 2015).
evidence: This is speculated based on simulation observations and cited behavior of another pore-forming toxin.

claim: The upward-tilt of one β-sheet edge would provide an excellent attachment point for the β-strands of non-inserted subunits at the membrane surface.
source: It would therefore provide an excellent attachment point for the β-strands of non-inserted subunits at the membrane surface, and may guide them towards the growing assembly and, eventually, into the membrane.
evidence: This is speculated based on observed structural features in simulations.

claim: High concentrations of prepore GSDMDNT on the membrane would promote assembly into full prepore rings before folding and inserting the continuous β-sheet.
source: High concentrations of prepore GSDMDNT on the membrane would promote assembly into full prepore rings before folding and inserting the continuous β-sheet.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations and kinetic considerations.

claim: The observed upward bending of the membrane into the prepore ring inside is consistent with a pull on the domain that has to unravel to form the membrane inserted β-barrel.
source: The observed upward bending of the membrane into the prepore ring inside is consistent with a pull on the domain that has to unravel to form the membrane inserted β-barrel.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations of membrane deformation.

claim: Locally confined adherence of many unfolded hairpins would destabilize the membrane within the ring, similar to how antimicrobial peptides are believed to facilitate pore formation.
source: In a process similar to how antimicrobial peptides are believed to facilitate pore formation, locally confined adherence of many of the thus far unfolded hairpins would destabilize the membrane within the ring (Flores-Romero et al., 2020).
evidence: This is speculated based on simulation observations and cited mechanism of antimicrobial peptides.

claim: The kink in the membrane at the inner edge of the prepore ring may facilitate the insertion of the β-strands.
source: The resulting kink in the membrane at the inner edge of the prepore ring (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) may facilitate the insertion of the β-strands.
evidence: This is speculated based on observed membrane deformation in simulations.

claim: The instabilities in the globular domains of the circular prepore assembly are likely coupled to strong membrane deformation.
source: The instabilities we see in the globular domains of the circular prepore assembly are likely coupled to this strong membrane deformation.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations of both instabilities and membrane deformation.

claim: The lipid composition has a crucial effect on the assembly of pore forming proteins on the membrane and the subsequent insertion of their pore opening components.
source: The lipid composition has a crucial effect on the assembly of pore forming proteins on the membrane and the subsequent insertion of their pore opening components (Rojko and Anderluh, 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Higher membrane fluidity should lead to easier insertion of the membrane penetrating components and facilitate the formation of smaller pores.
source: Higher membrane fluidity should lead to easier insertion of the membrane penetrating components and facilitate the formation of smaller pores.
evidence: This is based on established biophysical knowledge.

claim: Increased lipid order should facilitate the formation of larger pores.
source: By contrast, increased lipid order should facilitate the formation of larger pores.
evidence: This is based on established biophysical knowledge.

claim: The high cholesterol content makes the plasma membrane mimetic comparably stiff, which leads to slower diffusion and higher tension of the open membrane edge.
source: The high cholesterol content makes the membrane comparably stiff, which in turn leads to slower diffusion and higher tension of the open membrane edge.
evidence: This is inferred from membrane composition and biophysical knowledge.

claim: For typical experimental model membranes, edge tensions are expected to be about half of that of the plasma membrane mimetic.
source: For these experimental model membranes, we expect edge tensions about half of that of our plasma membrane mimetic (Leomil et al., 2021).
evidence: This is inferred from cited literature on membrane properties.

claim: Despite the lower edge tension in DOPC, small pores form faster and are more circular than in the more rigid plasma membrane.
source: By simulating the 16-mer arc structure also in pure DOPC, we could illustrate the potential effect of faster lipid diffusion: despite the lower edge tension, small pores form faster and are more circular than in the more rigid plasma membrane.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data comparing DOPC and plasma membrane mimetic.

claim: The plasma membrane of eukaryotic cells interacts with the cytoskeleton.
source: As further complications, the plasma membrane of eukaryotic cells interacts with the cytoskeleton and the bilayers used in AFM experiments are usually supported on a solid surface.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge.

claim: Single particle tracking, spectroscopic measurements, and MD studies showed substantially different lipid diffusion in the directly supported and the unsupported leaflet.
source: Indeed, single particle tracking, spectroscopic measurements, and MD studies showed substantially different lipid diffusion in the directly supported and the unsupported leaflet (Schoch et al., 2018; Otosu and Yamaguchi, 2018; Roark and Feller, 2008; Koutsioubas, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Interactions with cytoskeleton and solid support are expected to impact the pore assembly pathways, in particular by lowering the membrane edge tension and by slowing the dynamics in the membrane.
source: We expect these interactions to impact the pore assembly pathways, in particular by lowering the membrane edge tension, an effect amplified by dissolved molecules and proteins that preferentially bind to the open edge, and by slowing the dynamics in the membrane.
evidence: This is inferred from biophysical knowledge and cited observations.

claim: Certain detergents can lower the membrane edge tension by up to two orders of magnitude.
source: How strong these effects can be is impressively highlighted by experimental observations of certain detergents lowering the membrane edge tension by up to two orders of magnitude and by the fact that lipids purchased from different suppliers yield drastically different strengths of the edge tension, presumably due to impurities (Karatekin et al., 2003; Puech et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: Arcs may be artificially stabilized on a crowded membrane by contacts to neighboring GSDMDNT oligomers.
source: As an additional factor, arcs may be artificially stabilized on a crowded membrane by contacts to neighboring GSDMDNT oligomers (e.g., by forming stacked or interlocking arcs).
evidence: This is speculated as a possible explanation for experimental observations.

claim: These effects may explain the observation that arcs are quite abundant in experiments on GSDMDNT and other β pore forming proteins, yet above a certain size do not remain stable in simulations.
source: Together, these effects may explain the observation that arcs are quite abundant in experiments on GSDMDNT and other β pore forming proteins (Mulvihill et al., 2018; Mulvihill et al., 2015; Sborgi et al., 2016; Vögele et al., 2019; Leung et al., 2014), yet above a certain size do not remain stable in our simulations.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation observations and cited experimental observations.

claim: In coarse-grained simulations, a 14-mer inserted GSDMA3NT was found to break up and transition to a slit-like pore.
source: In coarse-grained simulations, a 14-mer inserted GSDMA3NT was found to break up and transition to a slit-like pore (Mari et al., 2022), similar to what we observed here in atomistic MD simulations of a GSDMDNT 16-mer.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior simulation work.

claim: GSDMA3NT rings in pore conformation remained stable in atomistic MD simulations, whereas prepore rings proved comparably fragile and broke up.
source: Also consistent with our findings for GSDMDNT, GSDMA3NT rings in pore conformation remained stable in atomistic MD simulations, whereas prepore rings proved comparably fragile and broke up (Mari et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior simulation work.

claim: Within 4 µs of atomistic MD, the membrane did not detach from the arc-shaped GSDMA3NT 7-mer to form a membrane edge.
source: Within 4 µs of atomistic MD, the membrane did not detach from the arc-shaped GSDMA3NT 7-mer to form a membrane edge (Mari et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior simulation work.

claim: The GSDMDNT pore is 60% more hydrophilic than the GSDMA3NT pore on the Eisenberg hydrophobicity scale.
source: On the Eisenberg hydrophobicity scale (Eisenberg et al., 1982), the GSDMDNT pore is 60% more hydrophilic than the GSDMA3NT pore (Table 2).
evidence: This is calculated from sequence data shown in Table 2 using cited hydrophobicity scale.

claim: The difference in hydrophilicity between GSDMDNT and GSDMA3NT is the most likely cause for the detachment of the lipid bilayer from GSDMDNT but not GSDMA3NT.
source: However, a large difference in the hydrophilicity of the pore-facing residues is the most likely cause for the detachment of the lipid bilayer from GSDMDNT but not GSDMA3NT.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of simulation results and sequence analysis.

claim: The differences between GSDMDNT and GSDMA3NT highlight how the physicochemical properties of the different gasdermins may be tuned to very specific membrane environments, cellular contexts or pore formation pathways.
source: Therefore, the difference between our results for GSDMDNT oligomers and those for a GSDMA3NT 7-mer (Mari et al., 2022) highlight how the physicochemical properties of the different gasdermins may be tuned to very specific membrane environments, cellular contexts or pore formation pathways.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of simulation results for different gasdermins.

claim: Unlike GSDMA3NT, GSDMDNT allows the formation of sublytic pores that facilitate nonselective ion flux and thus dissipate the membrane potential.
source: Based on the marked differences in hydrophilicity of the pore-facing side of the inserted β-sheets, it is tempting to speculate that—unlike GSDMA3NT—GSDMDNT allows the formation of sublytic pores that facilitate nonselective ion flux and thus dissipate the membrane potential, as seen in our simulations (Figure 4) and in experiment (de Vasconcelos et al., 2019; Rühl and Broz, 2022; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is speculated based on simulation data and cited experimental observations.

claim: In earlier atomistic MD simulations of PLY, inserted monomers were ejected from the membrane within 1 µs.
source: In earlier atomistic MD simulations of PLY (Vögele et al., 2019), inserted monomers were ejected from the membrane within 1 µs, unlike what we observed here for GSDMDNT.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior simulation work.

claim: Trimers and pentamers of inserted PLY formed narrow pores similar to the small GSDMDNT pores, but with a more circular shape.
source: Trimers and pentamers of inserted PLY formed narrow pores similar to the small GSDMDNT pores found here, but with a more circular shape.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior simulation work and comparison to current results.

claim: The globular backbone structure of PLY did not crack in earlier simulations.
source: However, the globular backbone structure of PLY did not crack in the earlier simulations.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior simulation work.

claim: PLY comprises only one domain, whereas GSDMDNT is made of four domains connected by disordered loops that act as flexible hinges.
source: Whereas GSDMDNT comprises only one domain, PLY is made of four domains connected by disordered loops that act as flexible hinges (Marshall et al., 2015; Lawrence et al., 2015; van Pee et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior structural studies.

claim: The β-sheet of PLY is about twice as long as that of GSDMDNT.
source: In addition, the β-sheet of PLY is about twice as long as that of GSDMDNT.
evidence: This is based on structural knowledge from cited literature.

claim: The flexible elements of PLY likely allow the globular domains 1, 2, and 4 to stay in tight contact with each other even when the inserted β-sheet is highly curved at its membrane-inserted tip.
source: These flexible elements likely allow the globular domains 1, 2, and 4 of PLY to stay in tight contact with each other even when the inserted β-sheet is highly curved at its membrane-inserted tip.
evidence: This is inferred from structural knowledge and comparison of simulation results.

claim: In atomistic MD simulations starting with a lipid-filled GSDMDNT 33-mer ring, a bicelle-like lipid plug detached from the protein and started to diffuse out of the pore region.
source: In our atomistic MD simulations starting with a lipid-filled GSDMDNT 33-mer ring, a bicelle-like lipid plug detached from the protein and started to diffuse out of the pore region (Figure 3).
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The process of lipid plug expulsion is in agreement with observations from AFM experiments, in which material initially filling CDC or gasdermin pores gets cleared over time.
source: This is in agreement with observations from AFM experiments, in which material initially filling CDC or gasdermin pores gets cleared over time (Leung et al., 2014; Mulvihill et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior experimental work.

claim: The lipid plug remained flat during the entire simulation and did not curl up into a small vesicle.
source: While the process of lipid plug expulsion is overall similar to what we saw earlier in coarse-grained simulations of PLY (Vögele et al., 2019), there is one notable difference: the lipid plug remained flat during the entire simulation and did not curl up into a small vesicle.
evidence: This is directly observed in the simulation data and compared to prior work.

claim: For the cholesterol-rich membrane, a higher bending rigidity is expected, which would explain why the plug stayed flat.
source: For our cholesterol-rich membrane, we expect a higher bending rigidity, which would explain why the plug stayed flat.
evidence: This is inferred from membrane composition and biophysical knowledge.

claim: GSDMD forms plasma membrane pores following a concentration-dependent kinetic model similar to what Gilbert and Sonnen, 2016 proposed for PLY.
source: Taking together all our results, we conclude that GSDMD forms plasma membrane pores following a concentration-dependent kinetic model that is similar to what Gilbert and Sonnen, 2016 proposed for PLY, but highlights the specifics of GSDMDNT pore assembly (Figure 6).
evidence: This is inferred from all simulation results and cited model for PLY.

claim: At low abundance of prepore GSDMDNT on the membrane, small oligomers dominate.
source: At low abundance of prepore GSDMDNT on the membrane, we expect that small oligomers dominate.
evidence: This is inferred from kinetic considerations and simulation observations.

claim: Eventual membrane insertion of small oligomers would lead to small sublytic pores that can account for the early ion flux observed experimentally.
source: Eventual membrane insertion would then lead to small sublytic pores (Figure 4) that can account for the early ion flux observed experimentally (Chen et al., 2016; de Vasconcelos et al., 2019; Rühl and Broz, 2022) and that could grow further by monomer addition and fusion.
evidence: This is inferred from simulation data and cited experimental observations.

claim: High abundance of prepore GSDMDNT on the membrane would tilt the kinetic balance towards the assembly of larger prepore assemblies all the way to complete prepore rings and the collective insertion of the full β-sheet.
source: By contrast, high abundance of prepore GSDMDNT on the membrane would tilt the kinetic balance towards the assembly of larger prepore assemblies all the way to complete prepore rings and the collective insertion of the full β-sheet.
evidence: This is inferred from kinetic considerations and simulation observations.

claim: The formation of large prepore oligomers and rings would be favored on membranes with abundant PI(4,5)P2 based on their preferential incorporation into GSDMDNT interfaces.
source: The formation of large prepore oligomers and rings would also be favored on membranes with abundant PI(4,5)P2 based on their preferential incorporation into GSDMDNT interfaces (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is inferred from simulation data showing PI(4,5)P2 bridging.

claim: Folding of the β-hairpins and insertion into the membrane are expected to happen in concert.
source: As a result of the ordering effect of the lipid environment, the enthalpic energy contribution of forming hydrogen bonds during folding, and the energy penalty associated with unformed backbone hydrogen bonds, we expect that folding of the β-hairpins and insertion into the membrane happen in concert.
evidence: This is inferred from biophysical principles.

claim: All MD simulations were performed with GROMACS version 2020.3 using the CHARMM36m forcefield, the TIP3P water model, and an integration timestep of 2 fs.
source: All MD simulations were performed with GROMACS version 2020.3 (Abraham et al., 2015) using the CHARMM36m forcefield (Huang et al., 2017), the TIP3P water model (Jorgensen et al., 1983), and an integration timestep of 2 fs.
evidence: This describes the computational methods used.
